players.product: Regulated electric service under the Very Large Customer (VLC) tariff, with new gas, renewable and battery generation and transmission built for Microsoft's data center campus in the I-94 corridor south of Milwaukee and the Vantage Data Centers / Oracle site at Port Washington, Wisconsin

quarterly_data.signal: WEC 10-Q: WEC has incurred significant costs to construct generation, transmission and distribution assets that will provide energy and capacity to Oracle America Cloud Services LLC (OACS), which will take service under the newly approved VLC and Bespoke Resources tariffs. Following a credit rating downgrade of its parent, the contracts require additional collateral, which increases as project costs are incurred; the peak collateral requirement is currently expected to be approximately $7 billion, and WEC fully expects OACS and its parent to provide it.

WEC 10-Q: Q2 2026 other operating revenues include a $10.8 million current return (carrying costs earned during construction of bespoke resources assigned to VLCs; $15.1 million in the first six months, none a year earlier). Large commercial and industrial electric sales were 3,292.6 thousand MWh in Q2 2026 versus 3,003.1 thousand MWh. Six-month capital expenditures were $2,079.9 million versus $1,530.5 million, driven at the Wisconsin segment by combustion turbines and LNG at Oak Creek, renewable energy projects and electric distribution.
quarterly_data.figure: $10.8 million bespoke resources current return; 6M capex $2,079.9 million

connects_to.relationship: Electric service and new generation for Microsoft's data center campus in the I-94 corridor south of Milwaukee (Very Large Customer tariff)

contracts.signal: WEC 10-Q: in May 2026 the PSCW approved the new VLC and Bespoke Resources tariffs; subsequent to that approval, Microsoft entered into a service agreement to obtain service under the VLC tariff.
